text: dsh-plugin-onenote 是适用于 DSH Web 客户端的 OneNote 集成，通过 DSH 工具和设置卡片连接服务。用户可用设备码登录并选择允许读取的笔记本；助手可以浏览笔记本页面、搜索标题和近期页面文本，并把单页转换为 Markdown，保留标题、列表和表格等结构。适合希望在 DSH 对话中查找个人或共享 OneNote 笔记的用户，需要可访问相应笔记本的 Microsoft 账户。

dsh-plugin-onenote connects OneNote to DSH Web through tools and a settings card. Users sign in and select readable notebooks. The assistant can browse pages, search titles and recent page text, and read a page as Markdown. A Microsoft account with notebook access is required.
想让 DSH 帮我查找 OneNote 里的笔记标题和内容
能不能在 DSH 里只开放我挑选的 OneNote 笔记本给助手读取？
I want to browse my allowed OneNote notebooks and read a page as Markdown from DSH.
dsh-plugin-onenote 的功能「搜索 OneNote 页面」：助手可在用户允许的笔记本中搜索，先匹配页面标题，再检查近期页面的开头文本，并返回可继续读取的页面结果。
dsh-plugin-onenote 的功能「按授权读取页面」：助手可浏览允许的笔记本与分区，并将单个页面转换为 Markdown；页面所属笔记本必须在用户选择的允许列表中。

dsh-plugin-onenote README · dsh-plugin-onenote：Read the Microsoft OneNote notebooks **you choose** from inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

Sign in once, tick the notebooks this agent may read, and everything else stays
invisible. The allow-list is enforced inside the plugin before any Microsoft
Graph request, so a page that tries to talk the model into reading another
notebook has nothing to call.

> 中文文档：[README.zh.md](./README.zh.md)

dsh-plugin-onenote README · What it looks like：The settings card (Settings → Plugins → OneNote) is the only place to sign in or
change which notebooks are readable:

```
┌ OneNote ──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Connected                                             │
│ Signed in as you@example.com        [ Sign out ]      │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Tools：The agent gets four read-only tools. None of them can sign in, sign out, or
change the allow-list — those are user actions in the settings card.

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `onenote_status` | Reports the account and which notebooks are readable. |
| `onenote_list_pages` | Browses allowed notebooks → sections → pages. |
| `onenote_search` | Matches page titles first, then the opening text of recent pages. |
| `onenote_read_page` | Reads one page as Markdown (headings, lists, tables, links, code). |
dsh-plugin-onenote README · Install：```bash
dsh-plugin-onenote README · From the plugin manager (recommended)：dsh plugin install hestudio-community/dsh-plugin-onenote

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Or from npm：dsh plugin install dsh-plugin-onenote
```

Then open **Settings → Plugins → OneNote** and sign in.

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Azure app registration：The bundle ships a public client ID so it works out of the box. To use your own
app registration instead (recommended for anything beyond personal use), create
one in about two minutes — no paid subscription is needed:

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Azure app registration：1. Open [App registrations](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade)
   → **New registration**.
2. **Name**: anything, e.g. `DSH-OneNote`.
3. **Supported account types**: *Accounts in any organizational directory and
   personal Microsoft accounts*. Choose a single-tenant option instead if every
   user is in one tenant.
4. **Redirect URI**: leave empty — the device-code flow needs none.
   *(Optional: if you configure a platform, choose **Mobile and desktop applications**
   and tick `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/nativeclient`).*
5. **Register**, then copy **Application (client) ID**.
6. **Authentication → Advanced settings → Allow public client flows** = **Yes**,
   then **Save**. Without this, sign-in fails with `unauthorized_client`.
7. **API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions**:
   - `Notes.Read` — read the user's notebooks
   - `offline_access` — keep the session alive between turns
   - `User.Read` — name the signed-in account
8. No client secret and no admin consent are needed for a personal account. A
   work account may need
dsh-plugin-onenote README · Troubleshooting: "missing 'redirect_uri' input parameter"：If Microsoft fails with `invalid_request: The provided request must include a 'redirect_uri' input parameter`:

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Troubleshooting: "missing 'redirect_uri' input parameter"：- **Cause**: At `microsoft.com/devicelogin`, selecting a Passkey / security key /
  Windows Hello shortcut directly without typing your username causes Microsoft's
  login service to misroute the device code flow into an interactive web flow.
- **Fix**: In the browser, **manually type your full Microsoft account email address**
  first, then click **Next** before completing authentication. Alternatively,
  open the verification link in an **InPrivate / Incognito** window.

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Troubleshooting: "missing 'redirect_uri' input parameter"：Then point the plugin at your app by adding a patch layer of your own:

```yaml

dsh-plugin-onenote README · ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml (applies to every profile) or the profile's cordis.patch.yml：- id: onenote
  name: 'dsh-plugin-onenote'
  config:
    clientId: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
    tenant: common
```

`config` replaces the row's config wholesale, so restate every field you need.
section: ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml (applies to every profile) or the profile's cordis.patch.yml

text:
dsh-plugin-onenote README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clientId` | the bundled public app | Azure application (client) ID. |
| `tenant` | `common` | Tenant id or domain. `common` accepts work and personal accounts. |
| `maxPagesPerList` | `100` | Default page cap for `onenote_list_pages`. |
| `maxPageChars` | `60000` | Default Markdown cap for `onenote_read_page`. |

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Where state lives：`$DSH_HOME/onenote/` (usually `~/.dsh/onenote/`), mode `0600`:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `tokens.json` | Access and refresh token. |
| `signin.json` | The pending device-code attempt, so a reload continues the same code. |
| `settings.json` | The notebook allow-list. |

Delete the directory to reset everything. Nothing is written into your
workspace.

dsh-plugin-onenote README · How the privacy boundary works：1. The allow-list is a list of notebook ids in `settings.json`.
2. Every read resolves the **owning notebook first** — from the page, the
   section, or the notebook itself — and asserts the allow-list before fetching
   content. Guessing a section id does not bypass it.
3. The agent tools cannot write the allow-list. Only the settings card can, and
   only through `POST /api/onenote/notebooks`.
4. The system prompt tells the model the readable notebook names and that
   everything else is unreadable by design.

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Notes on the Graph API：- OneNote does not support app-only authentication, so a signed-in user is
  required; `Notes.Read` is delegated.
- `GET /me/onenote/pages?$search=` was retired in 2024
  ([announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/onenote-get-pagessearch-api-deprecation)),
  so search lists page metadata per allowed notebook and matches titles
  locally, then reads the opening text of the most recently modified pages. That
  keeps the cost bounded and never leaves the allowed set.
- Page content arrives as OneNote's HTML dialect; `src/parser.js` converts it to
  Markdown without a third-party dependency and never downloads media.

dsh-plugin-onenote README · Development：```bash
npm test          # 99 tests, no network, no host required
npm run pack:check
```

The suite stubs `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (a host-provided peer) through a Node
module hook, so a bare checkout runs without installing the harness.
